fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Paul says, “Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.” (1 Corinthians 11:28) It's a look in the mirror before the table. The word is examine, and it comes before the eating and drinking. Paul asks it of each one.

Paul doesn't say honor. He says anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body “…eats and drinks judgment on himself.” (1 Corinthians 11:29) The condition is eating and drinking without recognizing the body. What Paul says comes on that person is judgment, not honor.

The text says the opposite of False. Paul says, “Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.” (1 Corinthians 11:31) He says “we,” so he's including himself. That makes this one True.

Right. Paul says, “If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment.” (1 Corinthians 11:34) That's his reason, in his words. The hungry one eats at home, so the coming together doesn't result in judgment.
That's it, baker. Paul says, “…your gatherings do more harm than good.” (1 Corinthians 11:17) He's not grumbling about a small thing. He says plainly that he has no praise to offer.

Yes, baker. Paul says, “…there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.” (1 Corinthians 11:19) The differences are there to show something, and what they show is who is approved. Paul doesn't say more than that in this verse, so I'll leave it right where he does.

Yep. Paul says, “…as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal.” (1 Corinthians 11:21) Then he adds, “While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.” Eating together is supposed to mean, well, together.

The text says the opposite. Paul says, “…as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal.” (1 Corinthians 11:21) He goes on, “While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.” So the meal isn't being shared.

The leaders aren't named here. Paul asks about humiliating “those who have nothing.” (1 Corinthians 11:22) Just before that he says, “While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.” (1 Corinthians 11:21)
Yes. Jesus says, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood…” (1 Corinthians 11:25) He says it when He takes the cup after supper. So He ties the cup to His blood and to a new covenant.

Paul doesn't use that word here. He says they “…proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.” (1 Corinthians 11:26) Each time they eat the bread and drink the cup, what gets proclaimed is the Lord's death. And that goes on until He comes.

Yes. Paul says, “…when you come together to eat, wait for one another.” (1 Corinthians 11:33) Plain and simple. Earlier he said that as they eat, each one goes ahead without sharing (1 Corinthians 11:21). Now his instruction is to wait for one another.
